what: Max RSS of the probe measured without a Python parent: /usr/bin/time -f %M around nice, ionice and the probe, run from a shell on 2026-11-06 (warm caches, no cap). The Python harness that produced memory.jsonl is itself about 10.5-13 MiB, and Linux keeps the larger of the pre-exec parent's peak and the new program's, so any harness reading at or below about 13 MiB is a floor, not a measurement.
note: Fixture A scans through the harness read 12.1-12.7 MiB and refreshes 13.1 MiB; those are the floor. The true values are at most those and, by the rows above, about 8.6 MiB (scan) and 10.7 MiB (refresh) on a 0.5 M-entry tree without many hardlinks.
